body: I've also encountered this multiple times in the past and found it very annoying. I think clicking on a new page should reset the layout to the default (i.e. centered).

I found this [comment in App.tsx](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/frontend/app/src/App.tsx#L780-L781). It looks like not resetting the layout to the default may be an intended design. However, I also think in MPA this design doesn't hold.

Yeah this is a bit in between bug and feature. I want to look at revamping page titles/icons/config a bit in Q4, so not sure if it makes sense picking this up before. Not that we end up implementing something now and then changing the behavior again a few months later.

This is also true for MPAv2.

```
import streamlit as st

def page_1():
  st.write("Page 1")

def page_2():
  st.set_page_config(layout="wide")
  st.write("Page 2")

def page_3():
  st.set_page_config(layout="centered")
  st.write("Page 3")

st.navigation([
  st.Page(page_1),
  st.Page(page_2),
  st.Page(page_3)
]).run()
```

We can either:
1. Change the layout to "centered" on page change
2. Wait for the script to finish, and reset the layout if necessary.

A part of me thinks we should do (1) for v1, and for v2 track the active script hash, and only reset it if the active script hash is not the main script hash.

Following @kmcgrady's example, here are a few more scenarios that seem inconsistent regardless of main or sub-pages:
1. If we don't `set_page_config` in page 3, layout remains **wide** navigating from page 2 to page 3.
    ```
    def page_3():
      st.write("Page 3")
    ```
2. If we `set_page_config` without the `layout` param, layout resets back to **centered** navigating from page 2 to page 3. (Makes sense with the [default value provided](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/blob/develop/lib/streamlit/commands/page_config.py#L123))
    ```
    def page_3():
      st.set_page_config(page_title="something")
      st.write("Page 3")
    ```

I find it more consistent for each page to manage it's own layout _state_. I.e. Don't apply one page's layout to another that just uses default layout. But if some interactions trigger a certain page's layout to change, that layout persists after navigating back to that page.

K just read through this again and I think I agree with y'all. So basically the behavior should be:

- In a single-page app, don't reset the layout to avoid flickering (I assume this is what the original comment in App.tsx means?). 
- In a multipage app and while viewing a single page, don't reset the layout (same as in a single-page app). 
- In a multipage app with v2 where `set_page_config(..., layout=...)` is called in the entrypoint file, don't reset the layout (same as in a single-page app). 
- In a multipage app (v1 or v2) when switching from one page to another and if `set_page_config(layout=...)` is called inside of the page, reset the layout to the default value (centered) and update it if `set_page_config` is called again. 

Does that sound about right?

Since there are a few different cases, would be great to get a demo app with all these cases, so I can check before we merge.
Here's a demo app we can quickly test a few scenarios with https://multipage-layout-fix.streamlit.app/ -- I'm working on attaching a WIP PR whl to it

issue.body:
## Describe your changes
This PR addresses 2 issues with layout in both MPA v1 and v2 --
* default page layout (centered) is not respected when navigating *from* a wide layout page
* when a page's layout is dynamic, e.g. changeable based on user interaction, navigating back to that page does not preserve the last set layout 

The proposed changes now preserve the layouts for each page in an MPA, by storing the mapping of `page script hash <> layout` in React state on page change. The layout of the page to be rendered will be looked up in every new session handling, defaulting to centered.


Demo: https://multipage-layout-fix.streamlit.app/

## GitHub Issue Link
#6237

## Describe your changes

This is a redo of #9723 -- the changes in `handlePageConfigChanged`, `saveSetting`, and `handleNewSession` are the exact same and their descriptions are accurate.

In this PR, I modified the logic in `handleNavigation`. (thanks to the solution from @kmcgrady) 
Essentially when `handleNavigation` gets called for the **entrypoint file** and current page script hash is NOT in `preferredLayouts`, it is possible that `handlePageConfigChanged` has been called prior and we have set the layout for `mainScriptHash` (because before navigation, the app has no knowledge of page script hashes of all sub-pages.) 
If this is the case,
```
!keys.includes(currentPageScriptHash) && keys.includes(mainScriptHash)
```
should be true and then we set the layout on the updated current page script hash.


## GitHub Issue Link (if applicable)
https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/6237

## Testing Plan

- Updated the E2E test case to include different cases in `handleNavigation`
